manufacturer: Duquenois-Levine Reagent — Standard forensic spot test for cannabis
validationStatus: Prototype — colour regions from UNODC ST/NAR/42 (2013) Table 3, Duquenois & Moustapha (1937), and Levine (1969) J AOAC. Purple-to-blue colouration in chloroform layer is presumptive for cannabis. Not a validated diagnostic instrument.

referenceCard.description: Software-rendered 8-patch digital reference card displayed on-screen.
referenceCard.printNotes: No printing required. Display on a second device beside the sample.

reactionWindow.observationNotes: The Duquenois-Levine reaction develops over 1-2 minutes. Capturing at multiple offsets gives the full trajectory, improving confidence in borderline cases.

captureInstructions: Step 1: Add 5 drops of Solution A (vanillin + acetaldehyde + ethanol) to a small sample.
Step 2: Add 3 drops of Solution B (concentrated HCl). Mix gently — purple colour forms if cannabis present.
Step 3: Add 5 drops of chloroform (Solution C). Shake. Purple-blue organic layer = presumptive positive.
Display the Digital Reference Card on a second device beside the sample.
The app captures at 0, 5, 10, 20, 30, 60 seconds to track colour development.
Keep the camera steady throughout the timed sequence.
safetyNotes: Contains concentrated HCl and chloroform. Work in a fume hood or well-ventilated area with PPE.
Chloroform is a suspected carcinogen and CNS depressant. Minimise exposure.
This test is specific for cannabis plant material (THC). Hash, resin and plant material all give positive.
A positive is presumptive only. GC-MS confirmation is required under NDPS Act provisions.
